title: xDrip confuses G5 with a G6 and performs a preemptive restart on day 9 as well as on day 6
body:
### Expected behavior
Dexcom G5 can be used in Native mode.  But, since G5 sends raw data, you can still access the calibration graph.  And xDrip removes "Initial calibration" from the menu after initial calibrations have been submitted and replaces it with "Add calibration".

### Your environment
The problem was observed with the February 11, 2021 release, and February 3, 2021.


### Actual behavior
Calibrations are sent to the transmitter and are accepted by the G5 transmitter.  However, xDrip logs show they are rejected by xDrip.
![tempFileForShare_20210216-234941](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51497406/108206590-96d7fa80-70f4-11eb-93a3-64454447f949.jpg)

Logs show calibrations have been rejected.
No access to adding calibration in the top left menu as only initial calibration is shown there.
No access to calibration graph.
Empty calibration data table.

The symptoms match the behavior of xDrip with a device that does not send raw data like a Firefly G6,

After installing the January 29, 2021 version, the problem was resolved. 


### Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Install xDrip release February 11, 2021
Start a G5 sensor in native mode
Apply initial calibrations
Check calibration data table, or check the logs.

@viq:hackerspace.pl reported this in the Gitter room.
Another individual reported it on facebook where the calibration graph being missing and the calibration data table being empty were reported.
The calibration rejection logs were reported by both users.

@Chris2001 If you don't enter the sensor code correctly, or if you enter 0000 as the code, you will be operating G6 in "no-code" mode.  In that mode, you will be asked to calibrate once a day.
None of this is related to this particular issue.

I didn't enter 0000, I started the sensor like always with a proper code that was acceptet. But after the preemptive restart (day 9) it now seems to be running in "no-code" mode. Sorry for the fuss, it really isn't a big problem. Everything else works just fine, also the precision is still very high.

I didn't know that was the case.  Thanks for reporting it.  
How did it behave before after a preemptive restart?  I have never had a G6 that could perform a preemptive restart.

G6 uses factory calibration, which only covers 10 days.
After restarting a G6, factory calibration cannot continue because there is no characteristic programmed for day 11 or 12 or 13 etc.
So, what you describe makes perfect sense to me.  After a restart, it automatically switches to no-code mode as factory calibration is not valid any longer.

> How did it behave before after a preemptive restart? I have never had a G6 that could perform a preemptive restart.

Sorry again for the confusion, I have an old 80... transmitter (cf. above) with replaced battery (firmware 1.6.5.25) ... with the preemptive restart you can do 'time travel' back to day 3, so it normally works flawlessly (it did before). So the transmitter really theoretically will work in *factory calibraton mode* until it fails. Normally sensors work for me between 15 and 25 days like that (after that the values get unreliable especially when there is sudden change, up or down).
The time travel capability may have been removed.  Although, I am not 100% sure.

I am closing this issue because I believe the original issue has been resolved.

I will be learning more about the time travel.  We can talk more about it here if needed in the closed issue, or somewhere else.
